issues.reason: 'the ashes' is a definite plural, which *Categorical statements* decides by determiner and grammatical number ('a definite / demonstrative / possessed plural ... takes a group witness — (GroupOf <group> <kind>)'), reinforced by the *Partitives* count/mass cue ('a plural/count "the Ns" → GroupOf'); (Member sk_ashes_1 ash) instead predicates ash-hood of the collection as an object, exactly the reading the plural rules warn against ('(GroupOf g student) says the members are students — not that the group is a student').

'the next ebb tide' is formed exactly as the licensed deictic constants next_summer / last_spring are — the next instance of a recurring cycle, anchored to speech time — and the deictic rule forbids minting an sk_ witness or Member atom for one, so the absent class atom is compliance rather than loss and 'next' is kept inside the symbol rather than dropped; and on the alternative event-noun reading the reviewer's own gap concedes that 'on <event-noun>' has no licensed carrier, which the calibration line makes acceptable improvisation since the atom is true and its bare-symbol filler is a licensed Time shape ('a deictic or named time stays a bare symbol').

gaps_confirmed: a temporal adjunct anchored on a recurring natural event ('on the next ebb tide') taken as an event-noun entity: Time terms are calendar / clock / deictic only, During is restricted to during / while / throughout, and Before / BeforeBy do not render 'on', so nothing carries simultaneity with an event-noun anchor
new_gaps: no test distinguishes a distributive from a collective predicate outside the reciprocal/aggregate list and bare 'together / jointly' marking — a plural subject acting on one shared definite object ('the villagers scatter the ashes') sits between the group-only event and the per-member (Implication (PartOf $x <group>) …) rule that a distributive predicate is said to require, and the instruction set decides neither
defect_summary: The compliant form is (GroupOf sk_ashes_1 ash) in place of (Member sk_ashes_1 ash) — the group witness the definite plural requires — with the Theme link and everything else unchanged.
notes: The reviewer's plurale-tantum gap is not a real gap: the count/mass split is explicitly cued by grammatical number, and 'the ashes' is plural. Future is licensed by the lexically-future 'next' adjunct and 'at sea' correctly stays a bare constant in the event Location.
